items.title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis
items.summary: arXiv:2611.20827v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When processor implementation details are unavailable, black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering helps security researchers identify hardware conditions related to security vulnerabilities. However, this process requires substantial manual effort to design experiments, develop test programs, and analyze results for each processor. We present ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates this process. ProcReverser uses execution feedback to improve experimental plans and test programs and identifies microarchitectural properties fro…

items.title: A Deployment-Oriented and Resource-Efficient Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Explainable DDoS Detection in Operational Technology Networks
items.summary: arXiv:2608.16769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid neural-symbolic detector of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on the availability of operational technology (OT) networks, designed for their resource-constrained gateways, and an evaluation matched to deployment. A compact gated recurrent unit (GRU) is fused at score level with a shallow, readable decision tree, and weight and threshold are selected on validation data under an explicit false-positive budget, whose attainment in finite samples is analysed. The evaluation on CIC-DDoS2019, Edge-IIoTset an…

items.title: A Forensic Analysis of Metadata and Information Leakage in Swedish Public Documents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates metadata and structural content leakage in publicly available PDF documents from 30 Swedish public-sector authorities. Using an automated collection pipeline and ExifTool-based extraction, 2,876 documents were analyzed and classified using an R0-R3 risk taxonomy. Results reveal that 48.4% of documents exhibit significant metadata exposure (R2 or R3), with significant variation across institutional tiers (p < 0.001). items.title: Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning for Fine-Grained Intrusion Detection: A Multi-Class Analysis in Heterogeneous Attack Environments
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a vital role in protecting modern network infrastructures. Although Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training without sharing raw network traffic, global models struggle with non-IID attack distributions. Moreover, practical security operations require fine-grained attack classification for targeted threat responses. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the convergence dynamics and performance of Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning (HPFL), which combines multi-tier aggre…

items.title: TIBECG: Temporal Information Bottleneck for Lead-Specific Demographic Privacy in ECG Waveform Release
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transmitting an electrocardiogram (ECG) waveform can expose demographic information beyond an intended diagnostic task. We evaluate TIBECG, an architectural temporal information bottleneck, on individual leads extracted from hospital twelve-lead recordings. A 2,302,337-parameter processor varies its latent length while retaining the same nine-score consistency objective, without age or sex labels in protector fitting. Across 6,386 recordings, ten folds, 12 leads and 21 lengths, retrospective selections retained at least 95% of each lead's clean…

items.title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Published face-privacy methods report protection above 90% against black-box recognition models. That number comes from an evaluation protocol with two independent defects, reported in a measure that cannot size either one. The input is wrong: methods published since 2022 feed the network the whole photograph, or a detector's box, where deployed systems detect, align to a landmark template and crop. items.title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study proposes an interesting approach for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, which integrates blockchain technology, federated learning (FL), and allocation optimization of latency and resources. The research evaluates the proposed system using various performance metrics such as packet delivery ratio (PDR), model accuracy, and latency and demonstrates its superiority over existing techniques. items.title: PSM: Prompt Sensitivity Minimization via LLM-Guided Black-Box Optimization
items.summary: arXiv:2511.16209v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: System prompts are critical for guiding the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet they often contain proprietary logic or sensitive information, making them a prime target for extraction attacks. Adversarial queries can successfully elicit these hidden instructions, posing significant security and privacy risks. Existing defense mechanisms frequently rely on heuristics, incur substantial computational overhead, or are inapplicable to models accessed via black-box APIs. items.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Continual Counting
items.summary: arXiv:2609.17650v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Binary Tree Mechanism is a standard algorithm for differentially private continual counting, but its complete asymptotic optimality under differential privacy has remained unresolved since its introduction. We resolve this question. For $0 \leq \varepsilon \leq 1$, we prove asymptotically tight lower bounds for $\ell_\infty$, mean squared, and maximum per-coordinate expected squared error simultaneously under all regimes of $0 \leq \delta \leq 1/4$. items.title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We audit instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog. The research question we answer with this experiment is which models disclose a protected secret embedded in the system prompt, and through which techniques. Each model guards a secret 16-character flag set in its system prompt, while an artificial intelligence (AI) agent (OpenCode, powered by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), steered by a human researcher, tries to persuade it to emit the flag. The flag was exfiltrated from 296 of the 363 models, plus…

items.title: CoordX Types: A Trustless, Swappable Type System for Shared Records
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16128v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The CoordX Protocol carries signed and encrypted entries between parties. It proves who wrote each entry and who had permission to write it. It does not say what an entry means. That task belongs above the protocol layer. This paper describes the CoordX type system, the layer that gives entries a meaning. A type is a short document that says how to read one part of a shared record: which entries count, what each position means, what a party may do there, and what a party must do next. items.title: ECGGuard: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting Codes
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13357v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, leaving patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking can embed this metadata in the signal, but conventional methods fail under time shifts, and high waveform similarity does not guarantee the same downstream diagnosis. We present \rev{ECGGuard}, a deep watermarking framework for single-lead ECG. A fully convolutional generator embeds the payload without signal quantization, a detector decodes the message…

items.title: Watermark Evidence under Open-Weight LLM Modification: Exact Bounds for Low-Rank Output Watermarks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models can continue generating after their released weights are modified, while a watermark verifier still scores outputs against the original base and marked models. We study how such modifications change the evidence available to an OpenStamp-style verifier. At each shared prefix, we represent the modification as a residual in the next-token logits. We derive an exact finite-vocabulary lower bound on the expected log-likelihood-ratio evidence under a residual-span constraint, along with a sharp span-only deviation bound. We…

items.title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. As these agents evolve into autonomous systems that execute commands, manage dependencies, access cloud resources, and interact with other agents, their security risks extend beyond incorrect code to actions with direct consequences for software systems. items.title: PersonaHate: A Scalable Persona-Based Data Synthesis Pipeline for Hate Speech Analysis
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hate speech remains a persistent and evolving threat on online platforms. The widespread use of large language models (LLMs) further intensifies this problem by making hateful content easier and cheaper to generate at scale. Although stronger hate speech detectors continue to be proposed, their performance remains uneven across target identity groups and different forms of hateful expression, partly because existing training data provides only limited coverage of these cases. items.title: Is 4-Bit Quantization More Than Noise to a Chat Model's Safety Behaviour? Attributing Behavioural Shifts with Matched Perturbations
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chat models on phones and laptops are usually 4-bit copies of the model that was evaluated, and audits of such copies disagree about what quantization does to refusal. A 4-bit build is one of many weight perturbations of the same size, so a change in its behaviour could come from its specific rounding error or from any perturbation that large. items.title: Dressed in Authority: Practical Black-Box Jailbreaking of MLLMs via Visual Trust Bias
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are rapidly advancing, yet their safety remains a critical concern, especially under jailbreak attempts. Existing MLLM jailbreaks either inject fragile adversarial perturbations into irrelevant images or synthesize toxic visual cues to achieve text-driven attack intents. In contrast, a more practical MLLM jailbreak emphasizes enhancing attack efficacy directly on naturally occurring harmful image-text pairs. items.title: From Attack Tree to Model Checker: Binding CAPEC Patterns to Verify Robotic System Security
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security-minded verification of autonomous and robotic systems presupposes an attacker, yet the path from a threat catalogue to a checkable attacker model is still traversed by hand. This research preview presents the theory and construction of a pipeline that mechanises it. items.title: How Well Is My Artwork Protected? Predicting and Tailoring Protection against Style Mimicry by Personalization
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protection tools add an imperceptible perturbation to each artwork so that a model personalized on it fails to imitate its style, and they apply one recipe, a protection method at a fixed strength, to every artwork. We find that the same recipe protects artworks very differently, well beyond the noise of personalization seeds, and that cheap signals predict this protection before any personalization. items.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents must act on information from untrusted emails, webpages, and documents. This creates a central security challenge: malicious instructions and legitimate task directives can arrive through the same interaction channel. Existing defenses are largely hand-designed and static, making further improvements dependent on repeated manual redesign. We introduce Evolution Under Fire, a staged framework that couples safety-harness evolution with adaptive stressor evolution. Utility-constrained, Pareto-scheduled tree search ev…

items.title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable honeypots to generate responses and deceptive artefacts on demand, yet existing approaches evaluate generated content one reply at a time and leave open whether artefacts that jointly describe a coherent event retain an attacker better than unrelated ones. This question becomes pressing as autonomous LLM-driven offensive agents emerge as realistic adversaries. items.title: ConfGuard: a physics-grounded reference monitor for predictive-maintenance large-language-model agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-language-model agents now close the industrial predictive-maintenance loop, reading sensor windows, retrieving procedures and dispatching work orders. Two attack channels meet there: injected text in a retrieved document can hijack the decision, and a bounded sensor perturbation can corrupt the remaining-useful-life estimate behind it. Recent agent defenses police data provenance and tool privilege but cannot tell whether a prognostic quantity is physically plausible. ConfGuard is a reference monitor with a physics-grounded policy. items.title: Missing Security-Fix Backporting for GitHub Actions Workflows
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22519v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GitHub natively supports workflow automation through GitHub Actions, now the dominant CI/CD tool on the platform. Yet keeping these workflows secure remains an ongoing burden: maintainers often patch a vulnerability on the default branch but leave the same flaw on the release and maintenance branches that downstream consumers continue to build from. Carrying a known fix onto these divergent branches, called backporting, is rarely done, and this paper presents the first large-scale empirical study quantifying the resulting gap. items.title: Propose with the Gradient, Accept with the Loss: One Hedged Attack for Pixel-Sparse Robustness
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A pixel-sparse adversary may change a few pixels of an image to any value. Robustness to such attacks is currently measured with an ensemble, sparse-AutoAttack (sAA), because its members fail in different places: sparse projected gradient descent (sPGD) trusts a first-order model that a full pixel change breaks, and sparse random search (Sparse-RS) ignores the gradient even where it is informative. items.title: HE-LRM: Encrypted Deep Learning Recommendation Models using Fully Homomorphic Encryption
items.summary: arXiv:2506.18150v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: FHE inference systems primarily target models with dense inputs, while Deep Learning Recommendation Models (DLRMs) contain sparse categorical features that require lookups into embedding tables. Encrypted lookups are challenging because indexing is not natively supported and must be expressed using SIMD arithmetic. A direct one-hot formulation does not scale. items.title: From Strategy Search to Policy Learning: MCTS-Guided Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Safety Alignment
items.summary: arXiv:2511.19218v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly power web-facing applications, including conversational assistants and content services, where open user interaction exposes them to diverse safety threats and adaptive attacks. In particular, jailbreak attackers repeatedly reformulate harmful requests to bypass safety alignment. Although existing studies have concentrated on defending dynamic jailbreaks, they often retain discovered attacks as flat samples and discard information about how those attacks were found. items.title: CyBiasBench: Benchmarking Bias in LLM Agents for Cyber-Attack Scenarios
items.summary: arXiv:2605.07830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in offensive cybersecurity. In this paper, we reveal an interesting phenomenon: different agents exhibit distinct attack patterns. Specifically, agents exhibit distinct attack-selection biases, differing in both the families they explore and the concentration of their efforts. items.title: LLM Misuse Safeguards Rely on Untrusted Input: A Widespread, High-Risk Vulnerability
items.summary: arXiv:2607.27951v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models now help professionals in fields such as cybersecurity and biology, yet the same answers would help an attacker. Deployers rely on misuse safeguards to keep such answers from attackers. We find that these safeguards share a high-risk vulnerability: they decide whether to release an answer from what users write, including the professional identity or purpose they claim, and anyone can write such a claim. items.title: IoMT-SecAlarmBench: A Semi-Synthetic Counterfactual Benchmark for Integrity Attacks in IoMT
items.summary: arXiv:2608.26416v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) combines clinical physiological data with cyber-system information, creating challenges in determining whether an abnormal reading reflects a genuine physiological event, a device fault, or a cyber-attack within the expected physiological range. items.title: rApp/xApp Attestation: A New Security Use Case for O-RAN
items.summary: arXiv:2609.24296v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The disaggregation and softwarization introduced by the Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture enable multi-vendor innovation but also expose the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) ecosystem to new runtime security risks. items.title: OverServe: Resource Amplification Attacks on SaaS Agents via Tool--Prompt Co-Design
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) are enabling software-as-a-service (SaaS) providers to automate longer business workflows with agents. In subscription-based SaaS deployments, model and tool calls consume provider resources without additional customer payments. Because the agent autonomously decides when to stop, a malicious tenant can send a prompt to the agent, exploiting its completion decisions to extend execution and waste provider resources. items.title: obfsgen: Generative Tunnel Obfuscation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.15019v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Encrypted tunnels are widely used to circumvent censorship, which has drawn censors' efforts to detect and block them. items.title: RustMC: Automated Verification of Real-World Concurrent Rust
items.summary: arXiv:2502.06293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: RustMC is a stateless model checker that targets push-button verification of unmodified concurrent Rust programs. As both Rust and C/C++ compile to LLVM IR, RustMC builds on GenMC which provides a verification framework for LLVM IR. This allows verification of Rust code and any foreign function dependencies. items.title: Visual Contextual Attack: Jailbreaking MLLMs with Image-Driven Context Injection
items.summary: arXiv:2507.02844v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the emergence of strong vision language capabilities, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated tremendous potential for real-world applications. However, the security vulnerabilities exhibited by the visual modality pose significant challenges to deploying such models in open-world environments. Recent studies have successfully induced harmful responses from target MLLMs by encoding harmful textual semantics directly into visual inputs. items.title: Angelfish: Leader, DAG, or Anywhere in Between
items.summary: arXiv:2509.15847v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To maximize performance, many modern blockchain systems rely on eventually synchronous, Byzantine fault-tolerant (BFT) consensus protocols. items.title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16066v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the average one-guess success probability of an adversary who observes the ordinary integer sum of a finite-support secret and an independent integer-valued mask, subject to an absolute-moment budget on the mask. items.title: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Much of the web is funded by advertising, a model that erodes as humans delegate browsing to AI agents acting on their behalf. A natural replacement is for agents to pay for what they consume, often a fraction of a cent per request. At the scale of web traffic, this could mean tens or even hundreds of millions of payments per second. We present Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments. items.title: From Token Changes to Task Failures: Bit Flips in a Shared KV-Cache Block
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In LLM serving systems with prefix caching, each KV block of a shared system prompt is held in GPU memory as a single physical copy, which every request with that prompt reads. items.title: TetherMark: Instance-Level Watermark Authentication Against Cross-Instance Transplantation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust watermarking is commonly verified by asking whether a hidden payload remains decodable after compression, geometric distortion, or generative editing. items.title: A Little Advice Suffices: Diffie-Hellman Is as Hard as Discrete Logarithm

items.title: auryn-docker 0.8.2
items.summary: Dockerfile plugin for Auryn and the first producer of the deployment & infrastructure tier (ADR 0007). A dependency-free Dockerfile parser emits BuildStage nodes, the shared image-keyed `Image` hub (the FROM chain, as resolved:false placeholders) and multi-stage COPY --from edges; a `deploy` enrichment links build stages to the code they package (PACKAGES), recomputes image `resolved` and GCs orphan images. Compose/k8s/Helm/Terraform producers join onto the hub. Depends only on auryn-core.

items.title: auryn-cuda 0.8.2
items.summary: CUDA language plugin for Auryn: a fast tree-sitter-cuda engine. CUDA is a superset of C++, so it reuses the auryn-cpp extraction engine verbatim (namespaces/classes/structs/enums/methods/fields/params, type hierarchy, templates, includes/macros, calls) and adds the CUDA-only graph signals: an `execution_space` property (`__global__`/`__device__`/`__host__`) and a LAUNCHES edge for `kernel >>` launches. A deep libclang/nvcc pass is the planned second phase.

items.title: auryn-csharp 0.8.2
items.summary: C# language plugin for Auryn: fast tree-sitter parse + deep Roslyn extractor (bundled source, built on demand; requires the .NET SDK).

items.title: auryn-cpp 0.8.2
items.summary: C++ language plugin for Auryn: a fast tree-sitter-cpp engine extracting namespaces/classes/structs/unions/enums (incl. `enum class`)/methods/fields/params/free functions, the class hierarchy (EXTENDS, multiple inheritance), templates, #includes/macros, and calls -- including out-of-line `Class::method` definitions resolved back to their class. A deep libclang engine (template instantiation, overload resolution, ADL, precise header linking) is the planned second phase.

items.title: auryn-core 0.8.2
items.summary: Core of Auryn: registry/plugin discovery, git+local sources, the FalkorDB graph layer, the MCP server, the viewer, and the `auryn` CLI. Language support ships as separate `auryn-` plugins.

items.title: auryn-compose 0.8.2
items.summary: Docker Compose plugin for Auryn (deployment & infrastructure tier, ADR 0007). Parses docker-compose files into Service nodes (RUNS_IMAGE the shared Image hub, DEPENDS_ON other services). A `deploy-compose` enrichment links each service that has both `build:` and `image:` to the Dockerfile stage it builds (`build.target`, else the final stage) with BUILDS_IMAGE, marking the image resolved/internal; the stages come from auryn-docker, so install both. Depends on auryn-core and PyYAML.
